name: Resistance Band Row
family: HROW (own parent card: content.md 2.3 ruling, floor-body contact does not match seated_cable_row's foot-platform)

claims.text: Sit on a mat with both legs out in front, feet flexed, and wrap the band around the soles of the feet, holding one end in each hand.

quotes.text: While seated on a yoga mat, extend both legs out in front of you with your feet flexed. Wrap the recovery band around the bottom of your feet so that you are holding one end of the band in each hand.
Sit on a mat with a resistance band around your feet.

claims.text: Check the band is in good condition and firmly anchored around the feet before starting; pressing the feet against something sturdy helps keep it in place.

quotes.text: Ensure that the recovery band is in good condition and securely anchored around your feet to avoid injury. You could also press your feet against a sturdy object to help keep the band in place.

claims.text: Sit up tall with the back straight and neutral, shoulder blades drawn down and back, arms straight in front holding the band with palms facing in.

quotes.text: Sit up tall and draw your shoulder blades down and back to push your chest out. Extend your arms in front of you so that you are holding the ends of the band with a neutral grip (palms facing inwards).
Keep your back in a straight, neutral position.

claims.text: Bend the elbows and pull them straight back, close to the sides, until you feel a small squeeze between the shoulder blades.

quotes.text: Using the muscles in both your arms and back, bend your elbows backwards to increase the tension in the band, ensuring that your elbows remain in close contact with the sides of your body. You should feel a small squeeze between your shoulder blades.
Hold onto either end and pull your elbows straight back towards you, squeezing your shoulder blades together.

claims.text: Breathe out on the pull, breathe in and straighten the arms under control on the way back.

quotes.text: Inhale. Exhale. Using the muscles in both your arms and back, bend your elbows backwards to increase the tension in the band
Inhale. Extend your elbows to return to the starting position.
Control the movement back to the start position.

claims.text: In Thera-Band and Cando elastic tubing, tension rose in a straight line with stretch once past a small initial threshold, and the start length sets the tension for a given stretch. Tubing measured in the lab, applied to the band by similarity: the pull gets harder toward the end of each rep, and the length of band held sets the load.

quotes.text: In an in vitro-series the tubing tension in relation to elongation of 6 colors of Thera-Band and Cando tubings was directly measured.
The tension/elongation relation is linear beyond a threshold in the early part of elongation.
The prediction of maximum tension values for any given elongation is possible by simple variation of resting length.

claims.text: In an isometric seated row the mid back (middle trapezius and rhomboids) was the most active of four pulls tested, with one of the highest lat-to-biceps ratios. Applied to the band row by similarity.

quotes.text: The highest latissimus dorsi to biceps ratio of activation occurred during the wide grip pulldown and the seated row. Highest levels of myoelectric activity in the middle trapezius/rhomboid muscle group occurred during the seated row.

claims.text: In a prone barbell row, the rear delts, biceps, lats and mid trapezius were all measured working. Applied here by similarity.

quotes.text: SEMG measurements were taken for the trapezius transversus (TT), rear deltoid (RD), latissimus dorsi (LD) and biceps brachii (BB).

claims.text: No band-row source gives seconds per phase or a pause. The plate's 2 seconds each way with no pause is a drawing convention that fits ACSM's moderate speed (1-2 s each way, advised for intermediate to advanced lifters working toward heavy loads) and the band sources' controlled return.

quotes.text: with eventual emphasis on heavy loading (1-6 RM) using 3- to 5-min rest periods between sets performed at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC)
Control the movement back to the start position.

claims.text: Band hand contact: secure the band to the hand before use so it cannot slip; a 'grip wrap' lays the band flat in the palm with its end toward the little finger, wraps the long end round the back of the hand, and then grasps firmly. Wrapping twice may help.

quotes.text: Your elastic band or tubing should be securely attached to your hand or foot before use to avoid slippage and possible injury. “Double wrapping” the band may help secure it to your hand or foot.
Lay the band flat in your hand with the end toward your pinky finger. Wrap the long end of the band around the back of your hand. Repeat as needed. Firmly grasp.

claims.text: Band thumb: in the 'palm wrap' the band ends start between the thumb and the palm, palms up; the palms then turn inward so the band wraps round the back of the hands, and the hands grasp firmly.

quotes.text: Begin with palms up and ends of band between the thumb and palm. Rotate your palms inward, bringing the band around the back of your hands. Repeat as needed. Firmly grasp.

claims.text: Band wrist (from the chair-seated band row, feet standing on the band; applied to the long-sit floor row by similarity): keep the wrists straight, in line with the forearms; the band lies flat, not twisted, and the load is set by where the hands grip the band ends.

quotes.text: Be sure to keep your wrists straight and in alignment with your forearm.
The band should be flat, not twisted.
Adjust the exercise band to a tension level the provides enough resistance by changing where your hands grip the ends of the band.

claims.text: Band hand fault: losing the grip (or the band breaking) lets the band snap back, toward the head or face in exercises where it points that way. Control the band rather than letting it control you, never let it snap back, and avoid over-bending joints.

quotes.text: snapping towards the face if grip is lost or if the band or tube breaks.
remember to control the band or tubing rather than allowing it to control you. Do not allow the band or tubing to snap back.
Avoid hyperextending or over-flexing joints when exercising.

plate.viewWhy: The elbow-back pull and the back line that carries the fault (c3) read from the side; the floor sit is drawn as the census floorsit pose.
plate.equipment: A resistance band looped around the soles of both feet (c1); no machine. Floor line.
plate.start: Sitting on the floor, legs straight out, feet flexed with the band around the soles (c1); trunk tall and neutral, shoulder blades down and back (c3); arms straight in front, palms facing in (c3).
plate.end: Trunk unchanged (c3); elbows bent and drawn back close to the ribs (c4); shoulder blades squeezed together (c4); band stretched.

checkpoints.label: Sit tall
checkpoints.what: Back straight and neutral, chest up, the same from start to finish.

checkpoints.label: Elbows to sides
checkpoints.what: Elbows travel back close to the body.

checkpoints.label: Band round soles
checkpoints.what: The band sits securely around the soles of the feet, feet flexed.

mistake.what: Slumping: the lower back rounds and the trunk tips forward while holding the band.
mistake.why: Both band sources ask for a tall, straight, neutral back; no study counts how often slumping happens.

tells.text: Small squeeze between your shoulder blades

grip.type: Neutral, palms facing in, one band end in each hand (c3).
grip.width: Set by where the band leaves the feet (c1).
grip.thumb: TheraBand palm wrap: the band ends start between the thumb and palm, then wrap round the back of the hand (c12). Manufacturer manual, not row-specific.
grip.handContact: TheraBand grip wrap: band flat in the palm, end toward the little finger, long end wrapped round the back of the hand, grasped firmly; secure it so it cannot slip (c11).
grip.wrist: Straight, in line with the forearm (c13; from the chair-seated band row, MECH).

setup.step: Check the band for wear before you start.
Sit on a mat, legs straight out, feet flexed.
Loop the band around the soles of both feet and hold one end in each hand, palms facing in.
Shorten or lengthen the band in your hands to change how hard it is.
Sit tall, shoulders down and back, arms straight in front.

posture.point: Back straight and neutral, sitting tall, all set.
Shoulder blades drawn down and back from the start.
Elbows pull straight back, close to the sides.
Small squeeze between the shoulder blades at the end.
Breathe out on the pull; arms straighten under control on the way back.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Slumping, with the lower back rounded, while holding the band.
handlingMistakes.fix: Sit tall first; if you can't keep the back straight, hold the band further along its length so it stretches less.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Using a worn band or one that sits loosely on the feet.
handlingMistakes.fix: Check the band before each session and anchor it firmly around the soles, or press the feet against something sturdy.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the arms back.
handlingMistakes.fix: Control the way back to the start.

rows.means: The fault to watch here is losing the tall, straight, neutral back.
rows.fix: Sit tall; hold the band further along its length so it stretches less.

risks.risk: Using a band that is worn or not securely anchored around the feet.
Holding the pull with a rounded lower back.

zooms.right: Band flat across both soles, feet flexed.
zooms.wrong: Band on the toes, about to slip off.

zooms.right: Sitting tall, back straight and neutral, while holding the pull.
zooms.wrong: Lower back rounded, trunk tipped forward.

zooms.right: Shoulder blades down and back at the start, squeezed together at the end.
zooms.wrong: Shoulder blades still apart at the end of the pull.

libraryDiff.why: exercises.json lists mid_back primary and lats, rear_delts secondary (kept: c4, c8, c9). biceps is added as secondary: the elbows bend against the band (c4, 'muscles in both your arms and back') and a prone barbell row measured biceps working (c9); tagged MECH.

notes: Census lists the contact as standing-feet, but the exercises.json alias ('seated band row') and census pose (floorsit) put this on the floor, so the contact is floor-body. The seated cable row's primary contact is foot-platform, so under content.md 2.3 this is its own parent card, not a difference card: the lines once inherited are written here as the band row's own lines (c3, c4). No band-row EMG study was found; all EMG claims are applied from an isometric seated row and a prone barbell row and tagged MECH. Colado 2010 (elastic tubing vs machines) was dropped: no line used it.

W1A band-hand claims (2026-10-02), added for LIB-7's band hand pair; no verified line was edited. Contact c11 (grip wrap), thumb c12 (palm wrap: band ends between thumb and palm), wrist c13 (straight, in line with the forearm), hand fault c14 (grip lost: the band snaps back). Neither source names which wrap to use for the row or the direction a wrist bends when the grip fails, so the band Wrong for the wrist stays a gap; c14 stays as a general rule to control the band and never let it snap back; its face-ward direction is not this row's (see gaps, F07). grip.thumb, grip.handContact and grip.wrist still hold the earlier archetype-default text; switching them to c11-c13 is left to the verifier and LIB-7. The BeWise (Utah) band guide was found but could not be fetched (proxy refused bewise.utah.gov; web.archive.org unreachable), so it is not cited. The theraband-manual title is descriptive: the PDF prints only 'Instruction Manual' and 'The Hygenic Corporation' (fetcher check 2026-10-02).

W1 fixer round 2026-10-03: F07: gap added for the row's most common band-hand fault and direction; the W1A note no longer calls c14 this row's directional fault. F15: c13 names its source setup (chair-seated row) and is tagged MECH. F16: grip.thumb/handContact/wrist now cite c11-c13, grip.claims adds them; theraband-manual kind guideline -> manufacturer; c11 'helps' -> 'may help'.
gaps: Most common band-hand fault and its direction for this row (F07): no source ranks band-hand faults, and c14's face-ward snap belongs to the manual's starred exercises, not to this row anchored at the feet. LIB-7 must not draw a face-ward snap as this row's hand Wrong.
